title: Study habits
scenario: A university is doing a survey about how students study. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Where do you usually study, and why do you prefer that place?
What kinds of things distract you when you try to study?
Some people think students learn better in groups. What do you think?
How do you think studying will change in the next ten years?

title: Free time
scenario: A student magazine is asking readers about free time. You will answer four questions from a reporter.
questions: What do you usually do on your days off?
Tell me about a hobby that you started recently or would like to start.
Do you think young people today have enough free time? Why or why not?
If you suddenly had a free month, how would you spend it?

title: Food on campus
scenario: A university is asking students about the food on campus. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: What do you usually eat for lunch on a school day?
How do you decide where to eat when you have a short break?
Some universities want to offer only healthy food. Do you think that is a good idea?
How might food on campuses change in the future?

title: Getting around the city
scenario: A city office is studying how people travel. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How do you usually travel to school or work?
Tell me about a time when your trip took longer than you expected.
Many cities want people to use bicycles more. What do you think about this?
If your city could change one thing about its transportation, what should it be?

title: Friends and communication
scenario: A university research group is studying how young people stay in touch. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How do you usually keep in touch with your friends?
Do you prefer to send messages or to talk on the phone? Why?
Some people say that technology makes friendships weaker. What is your opinion?
How do you think people will communicate with each other in twenty years?

title: Learning languages
scenario: A university is doing a study on language learning. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about a language you have studied and how you began learning it.
What is the most helpful method you have found for improving your speaking?
Some people believe that apps will soon replace language teachers. Do you agree?
Imagine that everyone in the world spoke one common language. What would be the advantages and disadvantages?

title: Work and study
scenario: A scholarship committee is interviewing students about working while studying. You will answer four questions.
questions: Have you ever had a job or volunteer position while you were studying? Please describe it.
What skills do you think students can learn from working that they cannot learn in class?
Some universities limit how many hours students can work. Do you think this is a good rule?
If you were advising a first-year student, would you recommend working during the first semester? Why?

title: Choosing a major
scenario: The career center is collecting students' views on choosing a field of study. You will answer four questions from an adviser.
questions: How did you decide what to study, or how do you plan to decide?
What do you think is the most important thing to consider when choosing a career?
Many people change their major at least once. Is that a positive or negative thing, in your view?
How might the jobs available to graduates be different in the future?

title: Sleep and schedules
scenario: A university health project is studying student schedules. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Describe your typical daily schedule during a busy week.
What do you do to stay focused when you are tired?
Some schools are moving the start of the day later to give students more sleep. What do you think of this idea?
If you could design the perfect schedule for students, what would it include?

title: Public spaces
scenario: A planning department is asking residents about public spaces in the city. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about a public place in your city that you enjoy visiting.
What makes a public space comfortable for people to spend time in?
Some cities are replacing parking areas with parks. Do you think this is a good idea?
How do you think public spaces will change as more people work from home?

title: Social media
scenario: A university is researching the effects of social media. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Which social media platforms do you use most, and how do you use them?
In what ways has social media changed the way you get information?
Some researchers say social media reduces people's attention span. To what extent do you agree?
If governments were to regulate social media more strictly, what effects might this have?

title: Environmental habits
scenario: An environmental group is interviewing students about daily habits. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: What have you done in your daily life to reduce waste?
What do you think prevents people from adopting more environmentally friendly habits?
Some people argue that individual actions matter little compared with the actions of companies. What is your view?
Suppose your city offered rewards for people who reduce their waste. How effective do you think this would be?

title: Decision-making
scenario: A psychology department is studying how people make decisions. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about an important decision you made recently.
When you have to make a difficult decision, do you prefer to rely on advice or on your own judgment? Why?
Some people claim that having too many choices makes decisions harder. Do you agree?
How might artificial intelligence change the way people make important decisions?

title: Traditions and change
scenario: A cultural studies project is collecting students' views on traditions. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Describe a tradition in your family or community that is important to you.
Why do you think some traditions survive for generations while others disappear?
Is it more valuable to preserve traditions or to adapt them to modern life? Explain.
How do you imagine your community will celebrate this tradition fifty years from now?

title: Learning outside the classroom
scenario: A university committee is studying education reform. You will answer four questions from a committee member.
questions: Tell me about something important that you learned outside of school.
What are the benefits of learning from experience compared with learning from teachers?
Some employers value practical experience more than university degrees. What is your opinion?
If universities were redesigned from the beginning, what changes would you suggest?

title: Volunteering
scenario: A university service office is studying student volunteering. You will answer four questions from a coordinator.
questions: Have you ever done volunteer work? Please describe what you did.
What kinds of volunteer activities do you think are most enjoyable for students?
Some schools require students to complete volunteer hours before they graduate. What do you think of this rule?
How might volunteering change in the future as more people work and study online?

title: Exercise and health
scenario: A campus health program is collecting information about student fitness. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How often do you exercise, and what kind of activity do you usually do?
What makes it easy or difficult for you to stay active during a busy week?
Some universities offer free gym memberships to all students. Do you think this is a good use of money?
If you were designing a program to help students become healthier, what would you include?

title: Travel experiences
scenario: A tourism research group is asking students about travel. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: Tell me about a trip that you remember well.
Do you prefer to travel with friends, with family, or alone? Why?
Some people say that tourism harms the places that people visit. What is your opinion?
How do you think traveling will be different for the next generation?

title: Reading habits
scenario: A library committee is studying how students read. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: What kinds of things do you read in your free time?
Do you prefer reading on paper or on a screen, and why?
Some people believe young people read less than they used to. Do you agree?
What changes might happen to books and libraries over the next twenty years?

title: Technology in class
scenario: A university teaching center is studying technology in classrooms. You will answer four questions from an adviser.
questions: Which technology do you use most when you study for class?
How does technology help you learn, and when does it make learning harder?
Some teachers ban phones and laptops in their classrooms. Do you think this is a good policy?
If you could add one new technology to every classroom, what would it be and why?

title: Managing money
scenario: A student services office is surveying students about personal finances. You will answer four questions from a counselor.
questions: How do you usually decide what to spend your money on?
What do you do when you want to buy something but do not have enough money?
Some people think universities should teach every student how to manage money. What is your view?
How do you think the way people pay for things will change in the future?

title: Housing choices
scenario: A city housing office is asking students about where they live. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Tell me about the place where you live now and what you like about it.
What is the most important thing to consider when choosing a place to live?
Some students prefer living with roommates, while others prefer living alone. Which do you think is better?
If you could design the ideal student neighborhood, what would it include?

title: Art and creativity
scenario: A university is conducting a study on art and creativity. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: Describe a creative activity that you enjoy or have tried.
How do you feel when you visit a museum or an art exhibition?
Some people say schools should spend more time on art and music. Do you agree or disagree?
How might technology change the way that artists create their work?

title: Shopping habits
scenario: A magazine is writing about how young people shop. You will answer four questions from a reporter.
questions: Where do you usually buy your clothes?
Tell me about the last thing you bought that you really liked.
Do you think shopping online is better than shopping in a store? Why?
What would you buy if you won a small prize today?

title: Weather and seasons
scenario: A radio program is asking listeners about the weather. You will answer four questions from the host.
questions: What is the weather like in your city in the summer?
Which season do you like best, and why do you like it?
Some people feel happier when the weather is sunny. Do you agree?
How would your life be different if you lived in a much colder place?

title: Family and home
scenario: A student newspaper is writing about family life. You will answer four questions from a student reporter.
questions: Who do you live with, and what do you like about your home?
What do you usually do together with your family on weekends?
Do you think children should help with the housework? Why or why not?
Describe the home that you would like to have in the future.

title: Daily routine
scenario: A university is doing a survey about student routines. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: What time do you usually wake up, and what do you do first?
Which part of your day is the busiest for you?
Some people like to plan every day carefully. What do you think about this?
If you could change one thing about your daily routine, what would it be?

title: Holidays and celebrations
scenario: A community center is collecting stories about holidays. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: What is your favorite holiday, and how do you celebrate it?
Tell me about a special meal that you eat on a holiday.
Do you think people spend too much money on celebrations? Why or why not?
How do you think holidays will change in the next twenty years?

title: Technology and privacy
scenario: A university is researching attitudes toward online privacy. You will answer four questions from a researcher.
questions: How careful are you about the personal information you share online?
In what ways have apps and websites changed the way people think about privacy?
Some people argue that companies should be forbidden from collecting personal data. To what extent do you agree?
If privacy continues to decline, what consequences might this have for society?

title: Work and careers
scenario: A career center is studying how students think about their future jobs. You will answer four questions from an advisor.
questions: What factors are most important to you when you think about a future career?
How has your education influenced the kind of work you would like to do?
Some experts claim that people will change careers several times in their lives. What is your opinion about this?
If many jobs were replaced by automation, how should governments respond?

title: Cities and rural life
scenario: An urban planning institute is researching where people prefer to live. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: Would you rather live in a large city or in the countryside, and why?
How do you think living in a city affects a person's relationships with others?
Some people believe that rural communities are disappearing. To what degree do you think this is a serious problem?
If you were responsible for improving a city, what changes would you make first?

title: Online learning
scenario: A university is evaluating its online courses. You will answer four questions from an education researcher.
questions: What has been your experience with online courses or learning videos?
In what ways does learning online differ from learning in a classroom?
Some educators claim that online courses cannot replace face-to-face teaching. How far do you agree with this view?
If universities offered all of their courses online, what would be gained and what would be lost?

title: Culture and globalization
scenario: A cultural foundation is researching how global trends affect local traditions. You will answer four questions from an interviewer.
questions: How are the traditions in your country different from those in other places?
In what ways have foreign films, music, and food influenced the culture where you live?
Some people fear that globalization is destroying local cultures. To what extent is this concern justified?
If you could preserve one tradition for future generations, which would you choose, and why?
